## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose bit-fields into a compact word, a common protocol task.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masking
- Bit shifts
- Width enforcement

## Code Example
```javascript
// C-like pseudocode for clarity
uint32_t packHeader(uint8_t version, uint8_t type, uint32_t length) {
  return ((uint32_t)(version & 0xF) << 28) | ((uint32_t)(type & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate inputs without branching?
- How would you extend to 64-bit headers with more fields?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a rotation primitive with wrap-around using only shifts and masks, including masking to handle large r and the n=0 edge case.

## Key Concepts
- Circular shift using (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))
- Masking r with 31 to confine to 0..31
- Edge-case n=0 preserves x exactly

## Code Example
```c
static inline uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t x, unsigned r) {
  unsigned n = r & 31; // 0..31
  return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you generalize to 64-bit rotates?
- What are the potential performance differences vs. compiler intrinsics like _rotl?
- How would you test across boundary values (r=0, r=31, r=32, r=33)?

Tests a crisp bit-twiddling trick: constructing a mask anchored to the least significant set bit, plus proper zero handling.

## Key Concepts
- Isolating the LSB with n & -n
- Mask construction via (lsb<<1) - 1
- Edge-case handling for zero input

## Code Example
```javascript
function maskBelowLSB32(n) {
  const lsb = n & -n;
  return n === 0 ? 0 : (lsb << 1) - 1;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt to 64-bit inputs?
- What are the potential pitfalls on platforms with different integer sizes?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests precise bit manipulations without branches, a common need in codecs and bitboards.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and masks
- Rotation vs simple shift
- Handling 0-31 safely without undefined behavior

## Code Example
```c
uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t x, unsigned k){
    k &= 31;
    return (x << k) | (x >> ((32 - k) & 31));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- What happens for k=0 or k=31? Explain results and edge handling.
- How to generalize to 64-bit values? Discuss performance trade-offs and compiler optimizations.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks understanding of 128-bit bit rotations using only shifts and masks, with a branch-free formula.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and modulo wrap-around
- 128-bit arithmetic and safe shifts
- Branch-free expression design

## Code Example
```c
uint128 rotateRight128(uint128 x, uint64_t r){
  r &= 127; // 0..127
  return (x >> r) | (x << ((128 - r) % 128));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for rotate left? 
- What happens if r is large or negative input?
